github-actions.description: Workflows live in .depot/workflows/ (Depot CI), which the manager's default patterns do not cover; the action.yaml pattern re-adds composite-action coverage in case patterns replace rather than extend the defaults.

packageRules.description: svelte-check, vue-tsc, and astro check embed the TypeScript JS compiler API, which typescript 7 (native) no longer ships; hold these at 6.x until the framework checkers support TS 7 (expected ~7.1). The Astro apps themselves are NOT held -- they run typescript 7, and the web-apps workspace root carries the 6.x that astro check resolves instead (see the bunfig.toml devDependencies note)

wrangler, @cloudflare/vite-plugin, and @cloudflare/workers-types all track the workers runtime (the plugin pins miniflare/workerd to a specific wrangler release; workers-types is generated from that runtime), so group every update type into a single PR that moves the cloudflare toolchain across all apps together
the @tanstack/ai packages (core plus framework bindings and adapters) release as a matched set, so group every update type into a single PR that moves them together

the tanstack router, start, and devtools packages release from shared monorepos and pin each other tightly (react-start pins router and router-plugin; devtools-vite ships alongside the devtools bindings), so group every update type into a single PR; the @tanstack/ai packages keep their own rule

group vite with the plugins whose majors track vite releases; @cloudflare/vite-plugin moves with wrangler, @tailwindcss/vite with tailwindcss, and @tanstack/devtools-vite with the tanstack devtools in their own rules
tailwindcss and the @tailwindcss scope packages (vite plugin, typography) release from one monorepo at a single version, so group every update type into a single PR that moves them together
effect and the @effect scope packages version against a shared core and release in lockstep, so group every update type into a single PR that moves them together

astro, the @astrojs integrations and adapters, and @astrojs/check version against astro core releases (spread across several repos in the astro org), so group every update type into a single PR that moves the framework together

svelte, svelte-check, and the @sveltejs kit and adapter packages track svelte releases, so group every update type into a single PR; @sveltejs/vite-plugin-* stays in the vite group because its majors track vite
vue, vue-tsc, nuxt, and the @nuxtjs modules move as one framework stack (nuxt pins its vue version and vue-tsc majors track the vue language tooling), so group every update type into a single PR

react and react-dom release in lockstep and their @types packages track the same major, so group major updates into a single PR; patch/minor stays in the weekly npm batch because the @types packages churn independently

the @sentry javascript sdks (astro, browser, cloudflare, react) release in lockstep, and warden -- the same org's review tooling -- is pinned twice (npm:@sentry/warden via the mise npm backend and the getsentry/warden action in the Depot workflows), so group every update type into a single org PR across all three managers
the @ark-ui packages (react, svelte, vue bindings) release as a matched set at a single version, so group every update type into a single PR that moves them together
the radix-ui umbrella package and the @radix-ui scope (primitives, colors) release together from the radix org, so group every update type into a single PR
the @fontsource and @fontsource-variable font packages publish from one monorepo and update as data-only bumps, so group every update type into a single PR
the @lezer parser packages (lr, highlight, and the per-language grammars) version against a shared core, so group every update type into a single PR
the @pierre packages (diffs, icons, theme, theming, trees) come from one org and are consumed as a set, so group every update type into a single PR

the unified markdown ecosystem (remark and rehype plugins, mdast/hast utilities, react-markdown, and their types) shares versioned interfaces across many small packages, so group every update type into a single PR
the @testing-library packages peer-depend on each other (react wraps dom), so group every update type into a single PR
alchemy and the @distilled.cloud provider packages (pinned via workspace overrides) must stay compatible with each other, so group every update type into a single PR
the @earendil-works pi packages (pi-coding-agent in mise; pi-ai left with Flue in 2026-08) come from one org and share the pi runtime, so group every update type across both managers
oxlint (mise), oxfmt (mise npm backend), and the oxlint-tailwindcss plugin all track the oxc project's release train, so group every update type across both managers
biome is managed by mise for the toolchain and pinned as @biomejs/biome in the legacy exercise workspaces, so group every update type across both managers to keep the versions aligned
cspell is managed by mise for the repo-wide spell task and pinned with @cspell dictionaries in the exercise workspaces, so group every update type across both managers to keep the versions aligned
the node runtime (mise) and @types/node track the same major, so group major updates across both managers; patch/minor stays in the per-manager weekly batches
the bun runtime (mise), the packageManager pin, and @types/bun track the same major, so group major updates across both managers
